original.guitar: Dann Huff and Biff Watson credited with riff and rhythm guitar on Come On Over (not broken down per track)
original.amp: Not documented. Late-90s Mutt Lange production: tight, polished rock crunch
original.effects: Short delay, small room (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From Come On Over (1997), produced by Robert John "Mutt" Lange; guitars tracked at Masterfonics, Nashville.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the main riff: tight JCM900-style crunch on the bridge humbucker. Play it with palm muting and stop the notes sharply, as the riff relies on the gaps. Channel B is a lighter AC30 crunch for the verses. Stomp the Tube OD for an even tighter riff.
recipes.why: Mutt Lange's productions use tight, polished rock guitars, the Def Leppard approach applied to country. A JCM900-style amp gives punch with a firm low end, and a very short delay and a small room keep the riff dry and in your face.

sources.title: Vintage King: The making of Shania Twain's Come On Over

original.guitar: Brent Mason credited with the licks and solos on Come On Over (not broken down per track)
original.amp: Not documented. Brent Mason's style: a clean, compressed Tele with a little breakup
original.effects: Compressor, delay, spring reverb (his typical style, not documented for this song)
original.notes: From Come On Over (1997), produced by Robert John "Mutt" Lange.

recipes.tips: Channel A for clean, snappy Brent Mason-style licks between the vocal lines, channel B for the solo. Pull the tone knob (single coil) for twang. Hybrid-pick and use pedal-steel-style bends. If the comp makes it feed back, drop Sens to 3.
recipes.why: Brent Mason's sound is a Tele bridge pickup, clean but compressed for sustain and snap, with a little breakup when he digs in and a delay behind it.
